previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant four months prior was admitted for evaluation of transient chest pain and low-grade fever. The chest pain, described as stabbing and distinct from his usual GERD, resolved spontaneously after aspirin. Workup including EKG, cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray, and lower extremity ultrasound showed no evidence of acute cardiac event, pulmonary process, or deep vein thrombosis. He remained afebrile during admission, and blood and urine cultures showed no growth. Anemia was stable and attributed to his transplant history. Liver function tests were normal, though a post-discharge sirolimus level was supratherapeutic, prompting anticipated outpatient dose adjustment. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on pending labs and continue all home medications without changes.

FINDINGS: The liver appears normal in echotexture without masses.  Pneumobilia

hepatic arteries were patent.  No fluid was identified in the abdomen.

Patency of the hepatic vasculature.  No ascites.  No intrahepatic bile duct
dilation.
